66113-wildwood-ways.title: Wildwood Ways
66113-wildwood-ways.creator: Unknown
66113-wildwood-ways.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. It was one of those days when the cart road from the north side to the south side of a pine wood leads you from early December straight to early May. On the one side is a nipping and eager air; on the other sunny softness and a smell of spring.

arxiv-1907-05118.title: R Melts Brains DOI: 10.1145/3359619.3359744 Conference: Proceedings of the 15th ACM SIGPLAN International Symposium on Dynamic Languages; 2019; Preprint Proceedings of the 15th ACM SIGPLAN International Symposium on Dynamic Languages (DLS ’19), October 20, 2019, Athens, Greece CCS: Software and its
arxiv-1907-05118.creator: Olivier Flückiger, Guido Chari, Jan Ječmen, Ming-Ho Yee, Jakob Hain, Jan Vitek
arxiv-1907-05118.description: Abstract . The R programming language combines a number of features considered hard to analyze and implement efficiently: dynamic typing, reflection, lazy evaluation, vectorized primitive types, first-class closures, and extensive use of native code. Additionally, variable scopes are reified at runtime as first-class environments.

arxiv-2106-00962.title: Convergent dynamics of optimal nonlinear damping control
arxiv-2106-00962.creator: Michael Ruderman
arxiv-2106-00962.description: Abstract Following Demidovich’s concept and definition of convergent systems, we analyze the optimal nonlinear damping control, recently proposed [ 1 ] for the second-order systems. Targeting the problem of output regulation, correspondingly tracking of 𝒞 1 \mathcal{C}^{1} -trajectories, it is shown that all solutions of the control system are globally uniformly asymptotically stable.

arxiv-2209-00760.title: Temporal Contrastive Learning with Curriculum
arxiv-2209-00760.creator: Shuvendu Roy, Ali Etemad
arxiv-2209-00760.description: Abstract We present ConCur, a contrastive video representation learning method that uses curriculum learning to impose a dynamic sampling strategy in contrastive training. More specifically, ConCur starts the contrastive training with easy positive samples (temporally close and semantically similar clips), and as the training progresses, it increases the temporal span effectively sampling hard positives (temporally away and semantically dissimilar).

arxiv-2306-17223.title: Critical accretion rates for rapidly growing massive Population III stars
arxiv-2306-17223.creator: Devesh Nandal, John A. Regan, Tyrone E. Woods, Eoin Farrell, Sylvia Ekström, Georges Meynet
arxiv-2306-17223.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Devesh Nandal, John A. Regan, Tyrone E. Woods, Eoin Farrell, Sylvia Ekström, Georges Meynet. Efforts to understand the origin and growth of massive black holes observed in the early Universe have spurred a strong interest in the evolution and fate of rapidly-accreting primordial (metal-free) stars.

arxiv-2312-11204.title: Hasse principle violation for algebraic families of del Pezzo surfaces of degree 4 4 and hyperelliptic curves of genus congruent to 1 1 modulo 4 4 Thanks: MSC 2020 : Primary 14G12, 14G05; Secondary 11G35, 14H25, 14G25
arxiv-2312-11204.creator: Kai Huang, Yongqi Liang
arxiv-2312-11204.description: Abstract . Let g g be a positive integer congruent to 1 1 modulo 4 4 and K K be an arbitrary number field. We construct infinitely many explicit one-parameter algebraic families of degree 4 4 del Pezzo surfaces and genus g g hyperelliptic curves such that each K K -member of the families violates the Hasse principle.

Amorín, John Chisholm, Matthew Hayes, Timothy Heckman, Svea Hernandez, Nimisha Kumari, Claus Leitherer, Crystal L. Martin, Michael Maseda,
arxiv-2403-08401.description: Abstract To study the chemical evolution across cosmic epochs, we investigate Ne, S, Cl, and Ar abundance patterns in the COS Legacy Archive Spectroscopic SurveY (CLASSY). CLASSY comprises local star-forming galaxies (0.02 < z < <z< 0.18) with enhanced star-formation rates, making them strong analogues to high- z z star-forming galaxies.

arxiv-2403-12204.title: Information Compression in Dynamic Information Disclosure Games
arxiv-2403-12204.creator: Dengwang Tang, Vijay G. Subramanian
arxiv-2403-12204.description: Abstract We consider a two-player dynamic information design problem between a principal and a receiver—a game is played between the two agents on top of a Markovian system controlled by the receiver’s actions, where the principal obtains and strategically shares some information about the underlying system with the receiver in order to influence their actions.

arxiv-2410-11964.title: A Complete Decomposition of KL Error using Refined Information and Mode Interaction Selection
arxiv-2410-11964.creator: James Enouen enouen@usc.eduDepartment of Computer ScienceUniversity of Southern CaliforniaLos Angeles, CA 90089-2905, USA, Mahito Sugiyama mahito@nii.ac.jpDepartment of Computer ScienceNational Institute of Informatics, SOKENDAIChiyoda City, Tokyo 101-8430, Japan
arxiv-2410-11964.description: Abstract The log-linear model has received a significant amount of theoretical attention in previous decades and remains the fundamental tool used for learning probability distributions over discrete variables. Despite its large popularity in statistical mechanics and high-dimensional statistics, the majority of related energy-based models only focus on the two-variable relationships, such as Boltzmann machines and Markov graphical models.

arxiv-2410-18390.title: Monolingual and Multilingual Misinformation Detection for Low-Resource Languages: A Comprehensive Survey
arxiv-2410-18390.creator: Xinyu Wang, Wenbo Zhang, Sarah Rajtmajer
arxiv-2410-18390.description: Abstract In today’s global digital landscape, misinformation transcends linguistic boundaries, posing a significant challenge for moderation systems. Most approaches to misinformation detection are monolingual, focused on high-resource languages, i.e., a handful of world languages that have benefited from substantial research investment.

arxiv-2511-08632.title: High-quality nanostructured diamond membranes for nanoscale quantum sensing
arxiv-2511-08632.creator: Alexander C Pakpour-Tabrizi, Artur Lozovoi, Sean Karg, Tecla Bottinelli Montandon, Melody Leung, Kai-Hung Cheng, Nathalie P. de Leon
arxiv-2511-08632.description: Abstract Deploying nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers in diamond as nanoscale quantum sensors for condensed matter and materials physics requires placing the NV centers close to the sensing target. One solution is to fabricate diamond nanostructures and integrate them with materials and devices.

arxiv-2512-11826.title: FSL-HDnn: A 40 nm Few-shot On-Device Learning Accelerator with Integrated Feature Extraction and Hyperdimensional Computing
arxiv-2512-11826.creator: Weihong Xu, Chang Eun Song, Haichao Yang, Leo Liu, Meng-Fan Chang, , Carlos H. Diaz, Tajana Rosing, Mingu Kang
arxiv-2512-11826.description: Abstract This paper introduces FSL-HDnn, an energy-efficient accelerator that implements the end-to-end pipeline of feature extraction and on-device few-shot learning (FSL). The accelerator addresses fundamental challenges of on-device learning (ODL) for resource-constrained edge applications through two synergistic modules: a parameter-efficient feature extractor employing weight clustering and an FSL classifier based on hyperdimensional computing (HDC).

britannica-1911-mieris.description: Article 'Mieris' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 18), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. Frans van Mieris, the elder (? 1635–1681), son of Jan van Mieris, a goldsmith and diamond setter, was born, according to Houbraken, at Leiden on the 16th of April 1635, and died there on the 12th of March 1681. His father wished to train him to his own business, but Frans preferred drawing to chasing, and took service with Abraham Torenvliet, a glazier who kept a school of design.

pmc-11536045.title: Mitochondrial aspartate aminotransferase ( maa1 ) inactivation causes glutamate-requiring glu1 mutation in Schizosaccharomyces pombe
pmc-11536045.creator: Kenji Kitamura
pmc-11536045.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Two genomic genes, which rescue ammonium assimilation defect in the glutamate-requiring Schizosaccharomyces pombe glu1 mutant, were identified. The maa1 , encoding a mitochondrial aspartate aminotransferase, is the causative gene of glu1 mutation because an inseparable linkage between maa1 and glu1 on the chromosome, and also the glu1 mutant strain has a nonsense mutation within the maa1 coding region, which is responsible for its defective phenotype. The yhm2 , a mitochondrial 2-oxoglutarate carrier, was also isolated as a weak multicopy suppressor gene.

pmc-11654141.title: How to deliver person-centred care for people living with heart failure: a multi stakeholder interview study with patients, caregivers and healthcare professionals in Thailand
pmc-11654141.creator: Alessandra Giusti, Panate Pukrittayakamee, Kamonporn Wannarit, Lakkana Thongchot, Satit Janwanishstaporn, Kennedy Nkhoma, Sridhar Venkatapuram, Richard Harding
pmc-11654141.description: ContextHeart failure has high, growing global prevalence, morbidity and mortality, and is a leading cause of death with serious health-related suffering in low- and middle-income countries. Person-centred care (PCC) is a critical component of high-quality healthcare and is particularly vital in the context of a serious illness such as heart failure.

pmc-12654366.title: Gut Bacteria Strategies of Hylurgus ligniperda F. (Coleoptera Scolytidae) in Adapting to Temperature Changes
pmc-12654366.creator: Huanwen Chen, Dan Xie, Lihong Jiang, Fang Niu, Xiaomei Wang, Yan Dai, Defu Chi, Jia Yu, Shuang-Jiang Liu
pmc-12654366.description: Insect establishment and dispersal are often influenced by temperature, with gut microbiota playing a critical role in host adaptation to environmental stress. This study investigated how gut bacterial structure and function in the invasive red-haired bark beetle (RHB), Hylurgus ligniperda (Fabricius) respond to temperature fluctuations, focusing on three core culturable bacteria: Rahnella perminowiae, Serratia marcescens, and Hafnia psychrotolerans.

pmc-12773573.title: Abstract 258: Comorbidities Associated with Exclusion from rtPA in Obese Ischemic Stroke Patients with History of Smoking
pmc-12773573.creator: Philip C Brewer, Dami T Ojo, Sahil Garg, Philip X Broughton, Thomas I Nathaniel
pmc-12773573.description: IntroductionRecombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rtPA) is the only approved treatment for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients, however, only a minuscule percentage of patients receive rtPA [1, 2]. In some cases, the reason for patients' exclusion from rtPA is due to risk factors and comorbidities [1, 2].

pmc-13163935.title: Gender Disparities in the Prevalence, Trends, and Determinants of Later‐Life Urinary Incontinence: A Disproportionate Burden on Women
pmc-13163935.creator: Xiyin Chen, Shaoxiang Jiang, Muqi Guo, Hao Zhang, Mouwang Zhou, Yao Yao
pmc-13163935.description: ObjectivesUrinary incontinence (UI) significantly deteriorates the quality of life in the elderly, with a disproportionately higher burden among women. With populations aging in the USA and the UK, understanding the gender‐specific prevalence, determinants, and future care needs in UI is critical for shaping gender‐responsive health policies and care strategies.

pmc-13191606.title: Photocatalysis beyond band gaps and hot carriers: toward a unified view of semiconductor and plasmonic systems
pmc-13191606.creator: Rishi Verma, Gunjan Sharma, Rohit Bansal, Charvi Singhvi, Saideep Singh, Vivek Polshettiwar
pmc-13191606.description: Photocatalysis stands at the forefront of efforts to address global challenges in sustainable energy and environmental remediation. In this review, we critically examine the two major classes of heterogeneous photocatalysts-plasmonic materials and semiconductors-highlighting their fundamental distinctions, catalytic mechanisms, and potential for driving light-induced chemical transformations.

pmc-13549508.creator: Tariq Parker, Odesanya Okikioluwa, Jolene Singh, Khalil St Brice, Felipe Ramirez-Velandia, Emmanuel Mensah, Theresa Williamson, Fedor Panov

pmc-13615104.creator: Charlotte Beaudart, Yveline Malréchauffé, Sophie van Heden, Dolores Sanchez-Rodriguez, André Scheen, Olivier Bruyère, Ali Mobasheri, Gustavo Duque, René Rizzoli, Jean-Yves Reginster, Jotheeswaran Amuthavalli Thiyagarajan
pmc-13615104.description: IntroductionGlucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, but their effects on musculoskeletal health remain completely misunderstood.ObjectiveThis systematic review/meta-analysis aims to synthesise clinical data on the effects of GLP-1 RAs on key relevant bone, muscle, and joint outcomes.
